{{Quote|I am Lord Gyaos Vader. I have your friend.|Gyaos Vader to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SW87" />}}
A [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifting]] entity known as '''Gyaos Vader''' lived in an [[Abandoned Kessel temple|abandoned temple]] on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] at the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Its true form was that of a flying, [[Bone/Legends|bony]] creature with [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavian]] traits. This mysterious being could metamorphose into the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Gyaos Vader was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in its Kesselian lair by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], a hero of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], some time prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Luke, it's Obi-Wan. I'm being held on Kessel. Help!|Obi-Wan Kenobi's distress call to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SW87" />}}
In the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Changeling/Legends|changeling]] named Gyaos Vader lived in an [[Abandoned Kessel temple|ancient temple]] on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]],<ref name="SW87" /> a barren [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="GATORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> In its natural form, this being looked like a [[Bone/Legends|skeletal]] [[Bird/Legends|bird]], but it could take the likeness of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]],<ref name="SW87" /> [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and second-in-command of the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="DBVader">{{DB|character|darthvader|Vader, Darth}}</ref>

Around [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Gyaos Vader captured the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and held him [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] on Kessel,<ref name="SW87" /> the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]]-shaped planet.<ref name="EGP">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> The young [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooinian]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who had began his [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]] under Kenobi, came to the rescue of his Master. Once Skywalker reached the creature's lair in the temple, he faced Gyaos Vader, who had taken the shape of the Lord Vader in order to surprise him. Both opponents drew their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] and engaged in a duel. During the [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|fight]], the creature turned back to its true shape and began flying around the room. Skywalker and the changeling traded several blows, but the young Jedi got the upper hand. Having killed Gayos Vader, Luke Skywalker freed Master Kenobi and set off for [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon]], where the [[Gold/Legends|golden]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] had been been taken hostage by [[Clados Vader|another shapeshifter]].<ref name="SW87" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Gaos_Vader.png|thumb|250px|Gyaos Vader in the 1987 ''Star Wars'' game.]]
Gyaos Vader was one of the stage bosses in the [[Wikipedia:Japan|Japanese]] [[Star Wars (1987 video game)|''Star Wars'' 1987 video game]]. The game featured various fake Vaders which were all revealed to be shapeshifting monsters. The canonicity of this game and the creatures it features is dubious. The room Gyaos Vader was fought in featured a [[Gold/Legends|golden]] mask<ref name="SW87" /> similar to that of the [[Wikipedia:Egypt|Egyptian]] [[Wikipedia:Pharaoh|pharaoh]] [[Wikipedia:Tutankhamun|Tutankhamun]].<ref name="Akhet">{{WebCite|url=http://www.akhet.co.uk/tuttreas.htm|text=Tutankhamun's Treasure|work=Akhet&mdash;The Horizon to Ancient Egypt|archivedate=20190715072156}}</ref>

According to both "[[Game On!]]," an article published in [[Star Wars Insider 135|''Star Wars Insider'' 135]], and the game manual, the fake Vaders ([[Clados Vader|Clados]], Gyaos, [[Sasori Vader|Sasori]] and [[Wampa Vader|Wampa]]) were "intended as illusions representing Luke's fears, like the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|Cave of Evil]] scene in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Empire Strikes Back'']]."<ref name="SWI135">{{InsiderCite|135|Game On!}}</ref> However, since those game opponents were able to kidnap Luke Skywalker's allies and hold them prisoner,<ref name="SW87" /> this article assumes they were real creatures rather than illusions. Additionally, the Vader-shaped figure that Skywalker fought in the Cave of Evil was more than mere illusion, being in fact a protean [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity known as the [[Dark Spirit]].<ref name="toy">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=Darth Vader (Dagobah)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjdagvader.asp}}</ref>

In the original game manual in [[Wikipedia:Japanese language|Japanese]], the character was called ''Gyaosu Beidā'' (ギャオスベイダー).<ref name="Manual">{{WebCite|url=http://www.videogameden.com/fc/extra/sta.pdf|text=Famicom ''Star Wars'' manual|format=pdf|work=Video Game Den|archivedate=20170105222157}}</ref> While ''Beidā'' is a transliteration of "Vader" in Japanese, ''Gyaosu'' and Gyaos refer to a number of giant, [[pterosaur]]-like monsters appearing in the [[Wikipedia:Gamera|Gamera]] film series from the [[Wikipedia:Daiei Motion Picture Company|Daiei Motion Picture Company]].<ref name="Gamera">{{WebCite|url=http://www.shrineofgamera.com/gamera.html|text=Gamera vs. Gyaos|work=Shrine of Gamera|archiveurl=https://archive.vn/Hv0P}}</ref>
